app.title: TestBoard PASKER ID
app.tagline: Where Pusat Pasar Kerja tests its services together: test scenarios, results, photo evidence and problem reports.

shell.projectArchived: This project is archived: everything can still be opened and reported, but nothing can be changed. A Super Admin can reactivate it.

roleHelp.TESTER: Runs the assigned test scenarios, records results and reports problems.
roleHelp.DEVELOPER: Sees reported problems, fixes them and updates the fix status.
roleHelp.VIEWER: Sees progress, results and reports without changing anything. Suits leaders.

systemRoleHelp.SUPER_ADMIN: Full power: invites users, configures the website, and everything an Admin can do.
systemRoleHelp.ADMIN: Creates and manages every project: phases, features, scenarios, tables, public view and problem review.
systemRoleHelp.NONE: Only opens the projects they are a member of, according to their task (Tester, Developer or Observer).

fields.title: Title
fields.name: Name
fields.severityHint: How badly users are affected. Critical: the service cannot be used at all.
fields.priorityHint: How soon it must be fixed. It can differ from the impact.

login.title: Sign in to TestBoard
login.demoNotice: Sample mode: this page uses sample data without a server, so nothing real is saved.
login.demoUser: You will sign in as {{name}} ({{role}}) in the sample project.
login.locked: Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.
login.noAccount: No account yet? Accounts are created by a TestBoard Admin. Ask an Admin for one.
login.remember: Keep me signed in on this device

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Choose a project to start working. Users only see the projects they are a member of.
projects.empty: You are not a member of any project yet. Ask an Admin to add you, or open My tasks if you are listed at a workshop table.
projects.emptyAdmin: Create the first project, then follow the "Start here" steps on the project home.
projects.welcomeAdmin: Choose a project to manage, or create a new one. Inside a project the menu on the left follows the order of the work.
projects.welcomeUser: Choose a project to start, or open My tasks to see everything assigned to you.

dashboard.title: Project home
dashboard.statusNote: Counted from the latest attempt of each test scenario in a test sheet. Retests are not counted twice; "Could not try", "Skipped" and "Not tried yet" never count as "As expected".
dashboard.noRuns: No test sheets in this project yet.
dashboard.noBugs: No problems in this project yet.
dashboard.noRunCases: No test scenarios have been scheduled in a test sheet yet.
dashboard.subtitle: Summary of the testing progress and problems in this project.

cases.title: Test scenarios
cases.subtitle: The steps to try and the expected results. Results are recorded in Test sheets or at workshop tables.
cases.empty: No test scenarios in this project yet.
cases.emptyFiltered: No test scenarios match the filters.

caseDetail.notUsed: This test scenario has not been used in any test sheet yet.
caseDetail.stepsPreserved: Step text is shown exactly as in the source.
caseDetail.archiveBody: The scenario is hidden from the active list. Its test sheet history and revisions are kept, and it can be restored.
caseDetail.archivedNotice: This test scenario is archived. Restore it before editing.

runs.title: Test sheets
runs.subtitle: A test sheet holds the scenarios assigned to individual testers. For group testing at tables, use Workshop & tables.
runs.empty: No test sheets in this project yet.

runDetail.casesHeading: Test scenarios in this test sheet
runDetail.snapshotNote: Title and version come from the copy saved when the scenario was added to this test sheet, so later edits never change past results.
runDetail.emptyFiltered: No test scenarios with this status.
runDetail.empty: This test sheet has no test scenarios yet.

confirmBody.ACTIVE: Once started, testers can record results. Test scenarios can still be added.
confirmBody.COMPLETED: Results can no longer be recorded until the test sheet is reopened.
confirmBody.REOPEN: The test sheet becomes active again so testers can retest.
confirmBody.LOCKED: A locked test sheet is final: results, test scenarios and assignments can no longer change. This cannot be undone.

notice.PLANNED: The test sheet has not started. Add test scenarios and assign testers, then start the test sheet.
notice.COMPLETED: The test sheet is complete. Reopen it for retests, or lock it once the results are approved.
notice.LOCKED: The test sheet is locked and final.

runDetail.addHeading: Add test scenarios to the test sheet
runDetail.addHint: Only Ready test scenarios can be added. A copy of each one is saved with the test sheet.
runDetail.addedSkipped: {{added}} added, {{skipped}} skipped (already in the test sheet or not Ready).
runDetail.removeTitle: Remove {{count}} test scenarios from the test sheet?
runDetail.removeBody: They can be added again later. The test scenario history is kept.
runDetail.removeBlocked: Test scenarios that already have results cannot be removed.
runDetail.removed: {{count}} test scenarios removed from the test sheet.

bugs.title: Problems
bugs.subtitle: Every problem found while testing or reported by users, with its fix status.
bugs.empty: No problems in this project yet.

bugDetail.noLinked: Standalone problem - not linked to a test attempt.
bugDetail.statusNote: The change is recorded in the status history with your name.

statusHint.VERIFIED: Make sure the retest result is "As expected". Earlier test results do not change.
statusHint.REOPENED: Explain why the problem is reopened, e.g. the retest is still "Not as expected".
statusHint.WONT_FIX: Explain why the problem will not be fixed.
statusHint.CLOSED: A closed problem can still be reopened if it happens again.

bugDetail.workflowHint: Flow: Open → In progress → Fixed → Ready for retest → Verified → Closed.
bugDetail.unlinkBody: The test result is not deleted; only its link to this problem is removed.

comingSoon.title: Coming soon
comingSoon.body: {{feature}} is built in Milestone {{milestone}}. See the roadmap in the README.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.body: The address you opened does not exist or has moved.
notFound.project: Project not found, or you are not a member of it.
notFound.item: This item was not found in the project.

caseForm.codeHint: Leave empty to generate one, e.g. UAT-AUTH-001.
caseForm.statusHint: Draft scenarios are not used in test sheets yet; Ready scenarios can be added to a test sheet.
caseForm.stepsHint: One step per line, starting with a number (1., 2., ...). Text is stored as written.
caseForm.versionNote: Saving creates version {{next}}. Test sheets already in progress keep their own version.

members.title: Members & tasks
members.subtitle: Who takes part in this project and what their task is.
members.emailHint: If this person has no account yet, you will be asked for their name to create one.
members.removeBody: Access to this project is removed right away. Their work history is kept.
members.readOnly: Only an Admin can change members and their tasks.
members.nameHint: There is no account with this e-mail yet. Enter the name and press Add to create one. The person activates it with an activation link.
members.notActivatedHint: The account was made from a name and e-mail; the person has not chosen a password yet.
members.adminsNote: Admins and Super Admins can manage every project, so they do not need to be added here.

projectSettings.moduleCodeHint: Upper case, no spaces, e.g. AUTH.
projectSettings.readOnly: Only Admins can add features and scenario groups.
projectSettings.moduleCodeEditHint: Existing test scenarios keep their current code (e.g. UAT-LPL-001); new test scenarios use the new feature code. Use the new feature code when importing.

profile.title: My profile
profile.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. A long sentence is safer than a short complex word.
profile.mismatch: The confirmation does not match the new password.
profile.passwordChanged: Password changed. Other devices have been signed out.
profile.demoNote: DEMO mode: password changes are not really stored.

devices.title: Signed-in devices
devices.subtitle: Devices that can still open your account without signing in again. If you do not recognise one, sign out all other devices and change your password.
devices.notRemembered: Signs out when the browser closes or after inactivity
devices.revokeBody_one: {{count}} other device will be signed out and must sign in again. This device stays signed in.
devices.revokeBody_other: {{count}} other devices will be signed out and must sign in again. This device stays signed in.
devices.revoked: All other devices have been signed out.

adminUsers.title: Users
adminUsers.subtitle: Super Admin only: create accounts, set their website role and help with account recovery.
adminUsers.tempPasswordBody: Shown only this once. Hand it over securely and ask the owner to change it in Profile right away.
adminUsers.deactivateBody: They are signed out of every device immediately and cannot sign in until reactivated.
adminUsers.forbidden: This page is for Super Admins only.
adminUsers.permanentHint: Owner account: nobody can revoke or deactivate it from the website.

cycles.title: Test phases
cycles.subtitle: A phase is one round of testing in a given period (e.g. UAT Stage 1). Test sheets and workshop tables always belong to a phase.
cycles.empty: No test phases in this project yet.
cycles.codeHint: Capital letters, digits and hyphens. Example: PHASE-1 or UAT-STAGE-1
cycles.dateOrder: The end date must not be before the start date.
cycles.editCodeHint: Letters, numbers, dot, dash or underscore (e.g. PHASE-1). Existing test sheets and problems stay linked to this phase.
cycles.statusConfirmBody: The phase status tells whether its test sheets and tables are being worked on. It can be changed again any time.

runForm.urlHint: Address of the site under test, starting with https://
runForm.invalidUrl: The URL must start with http:// or https://
runForm.created: Test sheet {{code}} created. Add test scenarios, then start the test sheet.

execution.newerVersion: The test scenario was updated to version {{current}} after it was added to the test sheet. This page keeps using version {{version}} so results stay consistent.
execution.noSteps: Steps are not numbered. Follow the step text above.
execution.actualHint: Required for "Not as expected". Describe what happened, not what was expected.

locked.PLANNED: The test sheet has not started. Results can be recorded once an Admin starts the test sheet.
locked.COMPLETED: The test sheet is complete. Ask an Admin to reopen it for retests.
locked.LOCKED: The test sheet is locked. Results cannot change.

execution.notAssigned: This test scenario is assigned to {{name}}. You can only record results for test scenarios assigned to you.
execution.notAssignedNobody: This test scenario is not assigned yet. Ask an Admin to assign it to you.
execution.readOnly: Your role can only view test results.
execution.bugsHint: A "Not as expected" result does not become a problem report by itself. Report a new problem or link an existing one.
execution.bugsNeedAttempt: Record a test result first to report or link a problem.

bugForm.fromExecution: This problem will be linked to {{run}} · {{case}} · attempt #{{n}}. The fields below come from that test result; review and complete them.
bugForm.titleHint: Short and specific, e.g. "Save button does nothing on the job form".
bugForm.assigneeHint: Only an Admin can assign a problem.
bugForm.lockedField: Some fields are locked because your role cannot change them.
bugForm.cycleFromRun: Leave empty to use the phase of the test sheet where this problem was found.

evidence.title: Photos & evidence
evidence.subtitle: All screenshots, documents and notes that prove the testing. Only project members can open them.
evidence.empty: No evidence files in this project yet.
evidence.deleteBody: An unused file is hidden and can no longer be opened.
evidence.uploadHint: Files uploaded here are kept as project evidence and can be opened by every project member.

imports.title: Import from Excel
imports.subtitle: Bring in many test scenarios or problems at once from an Excel file. Every row is checked first and you decide before anything is saved.
imports.drop: Drag an XLSX, CSV or JSON file here
imports.rules: Up to 40 MB · Excel (many sheets, embedded screenshots) · CSV template · AI JSON v1.0
imports.empty: No imports in this project yet.

fileError.TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED: The file must be XLSX, CSV or JSON.
fileError.SIGNATURE_MISMATCH: The content does not match the file type.
fileError.CORRUPT: The file is damaged or unreadable.
fileError.ACTIVE_CONTENT: The workbook contains macros and was refused.
fileError.DTD_NOT_ALLOWED: XML structure in the file is not allowed.
fileError.SCHEMA_MISMATCH: The JSON does not match the AI schema v1.0.
fileError.DEMO_XLSX: Excel import needs the server; in demo mode use CSV or JSON.

imports.targetQuestion: What do you want to import?

targetHint.TEST_CASES: A test scenario library, optionally with old UAT results (and screenshots).
targetHint.DEFECTS: Problems from a tracker: "Not as expected" rows and user complaints, with impact and screenshots.

importJob.sheetsHint: Select the sheets with the official test scenarios. Old versions or copies are better left out.
importJob.moduleHint: Used when a row has no feature column.
importJob.mappingHint: Unused columns are still kept as source data.
importJob.noHeader: No header found automatically; enter the header row number.
importJob.mode: When a test scenario code already exists

modeHint.CREATE_ONLY: Skip existing ones. Safe for importing the same file again.
modeHint.UPDATE: Filled columns overwrite the old content; a new version is created.
modeHint.NEW_REVISION: The definition is fully replaced from the file; a new version is created.

importJob.resultsHint: Status, date, tester name (as text, no accounts are created) and embedded screenshots go into a new test sheet. Test scenarios become Ready.
importJob.statusMapHint: Labels such as Closed/Open from Retest Status are never translated automatically; choose yourself or leave them without a result.
importJob.imagesAuto: {{count}} embedded images are linked to their rows automatically.
importJob.imagesReviewHint: These images are not on a test scenario row (e.g. a logo in the title area). Assign a row number or leave them out.
importJob.applyChanges: Apply the mapping changes and check again.
importJob.applyBody: {{create}} test scenarios are created and {{update}} updated. Invalid and duplicate rows are left out. Everything is applied at once.
importJob.applying: Applying the import… screenshots are being checked and compressed.
importJob.cancelBody: The uploaded file is deleted. No data changes.

done.PARTIAL: Import partly completed: rows with problems were left out.
done.FAILED: Import failed; no data was changed.

importJob.summaryRun: Test sheet {{code}}: {{executions}} results and {{images}} screenshots migrated

failure.COMMIT_FAILED: Something went wrong while applying; all changes were rolled back.
failure.INTERRUPTED: The server stopped while applying; all changes were rolled back.

importJob.noDataRows: No data rows below the header. Check the header row number and the selected sheets.
importJob.applyRun: Old results go into a new completed test sheet "{{name}}".
importJob.codeConflict: When a code is already used by another test scenario
importJob.codeConflictHint: E.g. the hidden "... 3" sheet uses UAT-LPL-001 for different content. New code = the next number in that feature; the original code is kept in the history.
importJob.conflictsHint: These codes are already used by test scenarios with different content. Decide per row, then press "Check" again.

reports.title: Reports
reports.subtitle: Summary of testing results and problems, data downloads and the project activity log.

filters.rangeInvalid: The end date is before the start date; the end date is ignored.

reports.how1: Each test scenario in a test sheet counts once, by its latest attempt. Retests are not counted twice.
reports.how2: Share as expected = the number of "As expected" divided by all test scenarios in the test sheets. "Not tried yet", "Could not try" and "Skipped" never count as "As expected".
reports.how3: Periods are calendar days in WIB (UTC+7): test sheets whose period overlaps, attempts tested and problems reported within the range.
reports.byTesterNote: Every attempt a tester recorded, retests included.
reports.defectsSummary: {{open}} open of {{total}} problems for these filters.
reports.empty: No data for these filters yet.

export.heading: Export data
export.description: The filters above apply. Times are in WIB.

results.title: Latest result per test scenario
results.hint: One row per test scenario in a test sheet: latest status, tester and linked problems.

attempts.title: All attempts
attempts.hint: Every attempt including retests, with result, tester and test time.

defects.title: Problem list
defects.hint: Problems reported for these filters, with linked test scenarios and test sheets.

cases.title: Test scenario library
cases.hint: Same format as the import template. Only the feature filter applies.

export.tooLarge: Too much data (more than 50,000 rows). Narrow the filters.
export.leadsOnly: Only Admins and Observers can export data.

activity.heading: Activity log
activity.description: Changes in this project are recorded automatically and cannot be edited. Visible to Admins only.
activity.empty: No activity for these filters yet.

adminProjects.title: Projects
adminProjects.subtitle: Every project on the website, archived ones included. The creator automatically becomes the project Admin.
adminProjects.createHint: You become the Admin of this project and can add team members afterwards.
adminProjects.codeHint: Capital letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen; 2-40 characters, e.g. KARIRHUB. Used in the project links; changing it later makes old links stop working.
adminProjects.name: Project name
adminProjects.archiveBody: The project can still be opened, reported and exported, but not changed until it is reactivated. Nothing is deleted.
adminProjects.empty: No projects yet. Create the first one to get started.
adminProjects.codeEditHint: Changing the code also changes the project's links; old links stop working. Existing problem codes stay as they are.

adminSettings.title: Site settings
adminSettings.subtitle: Apply to the whole website and every project. Changes take effect within seconds, no restart needed.
adminSettings.siteNameHint: Shown on the sign-in page and in the browser tab.
adminSettings.announcementHint: Shown as a strip above every page for all signed-in users. Leave empty to hide it.
adminSettings.defaultLocaleHint: For visitors who have not chosen a language yet.
adminSettings.supportContactHint: How to reach the administrators, shown on the sign-in page (e.g. team name and office WhatsApp).
adminSettings.sessionHoursHint: 1-72 hours. Applies to the next sign-in.
adminSettings.unusedFileDays: Delete uploads that were never used after (days)
adminSettings.unusedFileDaysHint: Evidence used in a result, problem or test scenario is never deleted automatically.
adminSettings.importDaysHint: Import history and per-row results are kept.
adminSettings.linkHoursHint: 1-168 hours. Applies to links created from now on.
adminSettings.rememberDaysHint: 0-90 days. Enter 0 to hide this option on the sign-in page. Remembered sessions do not time out after inactivity.

adminAudit.title: Site activity log
adminAudit.subtitle: Every change across the website: projects, user accounts and site settings. Cannot be edited.
adminAudit.empty: No activity for these filters yet.

request.title: Contact the administrators
request.subtitle: Only a Super Admin can help you recover an account. Your request goes straight to their list.
request.introPassword: Enter the e-mail of your account. After confirming who you are, an administrator sends you a link to set a new password.
request.introEmail: Enter your name and a way to reach you. An administrator will look up your account and tell you the registered e-mail.
request.contactHint: E.g. office WhatsApp number or another e-mail, so the administrator can confirm it is you.
request.messageHintEmail: E.g. your unit, your role in the project, or the e-mail you think you used.
request.tooMany: Too many requests from this network. Try again in 1 hour.
request.sentBody: If the details match an account, an administrator will contact you using the details you gave. Never share your password with anyone, administrators included.

reset.title: Set a new password
reset.containsEmail: The password must not contain your e-mail name.
reset.doneBody: Every device that was still signed in has been signed out. Sign in with your new password.
reset.askAgain: Ask the administrators for a new link with the "Forgot password" form.

problem.INVALID: This link is unknown or incomplete.
problem.USED: This link has already been used.
problem.REVOKED: This link was revoked by an administrator.

reset.activationIntro: Create a password for this account. Afterwards you can sign in with that e-mail and password.
reset.activationDoneBody: Please sign in with your e-mail and the password you just created.

dialog.title: Create a reset link for {{name}}
dialog.body_one: The link is valid for {{count}} hour and works only once.
dialog.body_other: The link is valid for {{count}} hours and works only once.
dialog.bodyNoHours: The link is valid for a limited time and works only once.
dialog.activeWarning: This account already has an active link. To never have two links for one account, the old link is revoked when the new one is created.
dialog.tipSend: Send it only to the account owner, through a contact you have verified.
dialog.tipOnce: The link is shown only this once. If it gets lost, create a new one (the old one is revoked).
dialog.tipWhat: When opened, the owner sees the account e-mail and sets a new password. All their sessions are signed out.

admin.title: Account recovery

admin.findHint: Find the account that matches the name and contact above, then link it.
admin.handledAuto: Resolved automatically: the password was changed with the link
admin.noteHint: Optional, e.g. "E-mail told via WhatsApp". Only Super Admins see it.

reasons.NOT_FOUND: not found, it may have been deleted or moved

bulk.noOpenRun: No planned or active test sheet yet

merge.archived: Archived and merged into the kept one

home.noRun: This table has no test sheet yet. Please contact the organisers.
home.featuresHint: Press the button on a feature to start. Progress is saved automatically.
home.noFeatures: The organisers have not chosen features for this table yet.
home.bugsHint: See problems from all tables, add "I saw this too", or report another problem.

public.howTitle: How to open this phase to the public

how.step1: Switch on "Show this phase on the front page" below.
how.step2: Tick the data the public may see (everything is hidden by default). A safe start: Feature list, Progress per feature, Problem list.
how.step3: Press "Preview public view" to see the result first, then press "Save public view" at the bottom.
how.step4: Done: anyone opening paskerid.kemnaker.go.id/testboard/ without signing in sees this phase. Signed-in staff can see it through the "Public site" menu.

features.intro: Features come from the scenarios in this phase's test sheets. Choose Done when finished, or Hidden to keep it off the public page. You confirm each change first.
features.confirmTitle: Change the status of feature {{name}} to "{{state}}"?

confirmBody.OPEN: The public page shows this feature as "To do". Tables keep working on it as usual. You can change it again at any time.
confirmBody.DONE: The public page shows this feature as "Done". Tables can still record results if something needs another try. You can change it again at any time.
confirmBody.HIDDEN: This feature is not shown on the public page. Tables and the big screen still show it. You can change it again at any time.

print.hint: Use A4 paper. Two cards per page; cut along the dashed line.
print.step1: Open the phone camera and point it at the QR code on the right.
print.step2: Or open {{address}} and type the 6-digit code.
print.step3: Try each scenario, then press As expected / Not as expected / Could not try.
print.qrLabel: QR code to sign in as {{name}}
print.keepSafe: This card is only for your table. Do not share it outside the room.
print.sheetIntro: Use it when the internet fails. Tick the results; the organisers will enter them into TestBoard.

sections.publik: Opening a phase to the public

flow.intro: TestBoard helps Pusat Pasar Kerja test services with users before the public uses them. The work always follows the same order, and the menu on the left follows it too.

cycle.title: Test phase
cycle.body: One round of testing in a given period, e.g. "UAT Stage 1, 3-4 December".

cases.title: Test scenarios
cases.body: The steps to try and the expected result. Write them one by one or import them from Excel.

plan.title: How to test
plan.body: A test sheet for individual testers, or workshop tables for group testing with QR cards.

test.title: Trying
test.menu: In a test sheet or on the table screen
test.body: Testers try each scenario and choose As expected, Not as expected, or Could not try.

bugs.title: Problems
bugs.body: A Not as expected result becomes a problem report. Developers fix it, testers check again.

report.title: Reports
report.body: A summary for leaders, downloadable as Excel or CSV.

flow.example: Example: the phase "UAT Karirhub Stage 1" holds 120 test scenarios. Ten workshop tables work on different features. Every Not as expected answer becomes a problem that an Admin reviews and a Developer fixes, and the progress shows in Reports.

signIn.intro: The sign-in page has two choices. Pick the one that fits you.
signIn.tableTitle: Table card: for participants at a table

tableSteps.title: Scan the QR on the table card
tableSteps.body: Open the phone camera and point it at the QR. You are signed in to the table right away.

tableSteps.title: Or type the 6 digits
tableSteps.body: Open Sign in, choose Table card, then type the 6 digits under the QR.

tableSteps.title: Tap your name
tableSteps.body: On the table screen, tap your name so answers are recorded under it. No e-mail or password needed.

signIn.userTitle: User account: for people with an account

userSteps.title: Choose User account
userSteps.body: On the Sign in page, choose User account.

userSteps.title: Enter e-mail and password
userSteps.body: Tick "Stay signed in on this device" only on a personal device.

userSteps.title: Forgot your password?
userSteps.body: Press "Forgot password?". Your request goes to the Super Admin, who sends a link to create a new password.

signIn.activationBody: If an Admin listed you with a name and e-mail, your account exists but has no password yet. Activate it in one of these ways:

activationSteps.title: With a link from an Admin
activationSteps.body: An Admin sends an activation link (e.g. via WhatsApp). Open it, create a password, done.

activationSteps.title: On the table screen
activationSteps.body: At a workshop table, press "Activate my account", choose your name and create a password. Only once.

participant.intro: You test together with your group at a table, from a phone or tablet, with large text and buttons.

steps.title: Sit at your group's table
steps.body: Each table works on the features the organisers chose.

steps.title: Scan the table card
steps.body: Point the phone camera at the QR on the card, or type the 6 digits under it.

steps.title: Tap your name
steps.body: Choose who is answering. You can change it any time.

steps.title: Choose a feature, then try one by one
steps.body: Follow the steps on screen, then press one of the three answer buttons.

steps.title: Tell us about problems
steps.body: Write what happened and take a photo of the screen. If another table already reported it, just press "I have it too".

participant.passed: As expected: the result matches what was expected.
participant.failed: Not as expected: the result is different or something is wrong. You will be asked to describe it.
participant.blocked: Could not try: the step could not be done, e.g. the page did not open.

faq.q: The internet dropped while answering. Are my answers lost?
faq.a: No. Answers are kept on the phone and sent automatically once the internet is back. An answer is never recorded twice.
Try the same scenario again and choose the right answer. The latest answer counts.

faq.q: My name is not in the list.
faq.a: Press "Change member names" and add your name. Names with an account (listed by the organisers) cannot be changed at the table.

faq.q: The table card does not work.
faq.a: Cards only work during the workshop. If it has ended or was blocked, ask the organisers for a new card.

tester.intro: As a Tester you try the scenarios assigned to you and report the problems you find.

steps.title: Open My tasks
steps.body: All your work is there: the tables you are listed at, the test sheets assigned to you, and the problems you reported.

steps.title: Continue a test sheet
steps.body: Press "Continue" to open the next scenario not tried yet.

steps.title: Record the result
steps.body: Choose As expected, Not as expected, or Could not try. For Not as expected, describe what happened and attach a screenshot.

steps.title: Report a problem
steps.body: From a Not as expected result, press "Report a problem". It is filled in from your attempt.

steps.title: Check again after a fix
steps.body: When a problem is Ready to retest, try the scenario again and mark it Checked, all good or Came back.

admin.intro: As an Admin you prepare and manage projects. Follow the "Start here" card on the project home; the steps are the same as below.

steps.title: Create a project
steps.body: On the Projects page, press "Create project". Enter a short code (e.g. KARIRHUB) and a name.

steps.title: Create a test phase
steps.body: Menu 1. Preparation › Test phases. Enter a name and period, e.g. "UAT Stage 1".

steps.title: Prepare test scenarios
steps.body: Write them one by one in Test scenarios, or bring many at once with Import from Excel. Every row is checked before it is saved.

steps.title: Choose how to test
steps.body: Create a Test sheet for individual testers and assign its scenarios. For a workshop, open Workshop & tables, create tables, enter the members' names (and e-mails if any), then print the table cards.

steps.title: Add people
steps.body: Menu 4. Settings › Members & tasks. An e-mail is enough; without an account, enter the name and send an activation link with the "Activation link" button.

steps.title: Follow up and review
steps.body: While testing runs, watch the Workshop & tables board, review incoming Problems, then share the Reports with leaders.

tips: Codes (project, phase, feature) can be changed any time; old links keep pointing to the same data.
Important changes, such as changing someone's task or locking a test sheet, always ask for confirmation.
The Help button at the top right explains the page you are on.

developer.intro: As a Developer you follow up on reported problems.

steps.title: Open Problems
steps.body: Filter by impact or by what is assigned to you.

steps.title: Start fixing
steps.body: Set the status to Being fixed so the team knows it is handled.

steps.title: Mark it fixed
steps.body: When done, set it to Fixed then Ready to retest, and enter the fix version.

steps.title: Wait for the retest
steps.body: A tester checks again. If it still happens, the status becomes Came back and returns to you.

observer.intro: As an Observer you see all progress without changing anything. Suits leaders.

steps.title: Project home
steps.body: How many scenarios were tried, the share of As expected, and open problems by impact.

steps.title: Reports
steps.body: Details per feature, per test sheet and per tester, downloadable as Excel or CSV.

steps.title: Problems
steps.body: The problem list with statuses; open one to see its history and photo evidence.

steps.title: Public page
steps.body: When a phase is public, its progress can also be seen without signing in.

roles.intro: There are three levels of roles. Visitors of the public page and table cards are not users.

rows.can: Everything an Admin can do, plus creating user accounts and setting their roles, website settings, account recovery and the website activity log.
Creates and manages every project: phases, scenarios, imports, workshop tables, public view, problem review, members and their tasks.

rows.who: Testers, workshop participants with an account
rows.can: Tries the assigned scenarios, records results and reports problems in the projects they belong to.
Sees problems and updates their fix status.
Sees all progress, results and reports without changing anything, and downloads reports.

publish.intro: Each phase can be opened to the public (no sign-in). Everything is hidden by default; an Admin chooses which data may be seen.

steps.title: Open Workshop & tables
steps.body: Choose the phase, then open the Public view tab.

steps.title: Choose the data to show
steps.body: Each item has its own switch. Items that may hold personal data are marked.

steps.title: Preview
steps.body: Press "Preview the public view" to see exactly what the public sees.

steps.title: Switch on and save
steps.body: Turn on "Show publicly", then save. The phase appears on the front page.

publish.sees: Visitors only see the data that is switched on, never anything else.

superAdmin.intro: The Super Admin manages the website as a whole.

steps.title: Users
steps.body: Create accounts and choose their role: User, Admin or Super Admin. Role changes always ask for confirmation.

steps.title: Account recovery
steps.body: "Forgot password" and "Forgot e-mail" requests arrive here. Create a reset link after checking who is asking.

steps.title: Website settings
steps.body: Site name, an announcement on every page, the help contact and sign-in time limits.

steps.title: Activity log
steps.body: A record of who did what and when, across the website.

glossary.intro: Terms used in TestBoard, with the original English term.

rows.meaning: One round of testing in a given period.
The steps to try and the expected result.
A part of the service under test, e.g. Job reports.
A set of scenarios within one feature, e.g. per sub-menu.
The scenarios assigned to be tried in a phase.
Group testing per table with QR cards.
A card with a QR and 6 digits to open the table screen.

rows.term: As expected / Not as expected / Could not try

rows.meaning: Something that does not work as it should.
How badly users are affected: Critical, Severe, Moderate, Minor.
How soon it must be fixed: Right away, High, Medium, Low.
Trying again after a problem was fixed.
Screenshots, documents or notes that prove a result.

points: Project data can only be opened by project members. The public page only shows data an Admin switched on.
A table card only opens the table screen, never other data, and only while it is valid.
The table screen never shows members' full e-mails.
Passwords are stored scrambled (hashed). Nobody, including Admins, can see them.
Photos and files are checked and made smaller automatically, and only project members can open them.

signIn.choose: Choose the way that fits you.

meja.title: Table card
meja.who: For participants testing at a group table. No e-mail or password.

pengguna.title: User account
pengguna.who: For Admins, Testers, Developers and Observers who have an account.

user.intro: Sign in with your account e-mail and password.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.body: In TestBoard, the Pusat Pasar Kerja team and participants try services together, record the results and report problems before the public uses them.

activation.title: Activation link for {{name}}
activation.intro: Give this link to the person. With it they choose their own password and can then sign in with their e-mail.
activation.whatsappText: Hello {{name}}, here is the link to activate your TestBoard PASKER ID account. Open it and choose your own password: {{url}} (valid until {{until}}).
activation.note: The link is only shown here. If it is lost or expires, create a new one; the old link stops working.

tasks.title: My tasks
tasks.subtitle: Everything assigned to you, across all projects you are a member of.
tasks.tablesHint: Tables where you are listed. Open a table to test together with your group.
tasks.openBody: This device switches to the table screen with {{name}} already chosen. Your account signs out of this device; sign in again any time with your e-mail and password.
tasks.runsHint: Scenarios you should try yourself and record the results of.
tasks.bugLine: {{open}} still being handled out of {{total}} reports
tasks.empty: No table or scenario is assigned to you yet. An Admin will add you to a table or assign test scenarios.
tasks.footer: Only your own tasks are shown here. Other people's tasks are not.

startHere.title: Start here
startHere.subtitle: Follow these steps from top to bottom. {{done}} of {{total}} preparation steps are done.

cycle.title: Create a test phase
cycle.body: A phase is one round of testing, e.g. "UAT Stage 1, 3-4 December".

cases.title: Prepare test scenarios
cases.body: Write the steps to try and the expected result, one by one or all at once from Excel.

plan.title: Choose how to test
plan.body: A test sheet for individual testers, or workshop tables for group testing with QR cards.

test.title: Run the tests
test.body: Testers try each scenario and choose As expected, Not as expected, or Could not try.

report.title: See the reports
report.body: A summary for leaders, downloadable as Excel or CSV.

TESTER.title: Your task: Tester
TESTER.body: Try the scenarios assigned to you, record the results and report any problem. All your work is on the My tasks page.

DEVELOPER.title: Your task: Developer
DEVELOPER.body: See the reported problems, fix them, then set their status to Fixed so testers can retest.

VIEWER.title: Your task: Observer
VIEWER.body: You can see all progress, results and reports of this project without changing anything. The summary is below; full reports can be downloaded.

projects.title: Projects
projects.what: The projects you can open. One project is usually one service under test, e.g. Karirhub.
steps: Press Open project to enter.
Admins can create a project with Create project.
Open My tasks to see all your work.

tasks.title: My tasks
tasks.what: Everything assigned to you across projects: workshop tables, test sheets and the problems you reported.
steps: Press Open this table to test with your group; your name is chosen already.
Press Continue to try the next scenario of a test sheet.
Press View to follow the problems you reported.

profile.title: My profile
profile.what: Your name, language, password and the devices signed in with your account.
steps: Change your password regularly.
Sign out devices you do not recognise.

dashboard.title: Project home
dashboard.what: A summary of the project: how many scenarios were tried, how many were as expected, and the problems still open.
steps: Admins: follow the Start here card from top to bottom.
Filter by test sheet to see one round only.
Press a number or chart to open the details.

cycles.title: Test phases
cycles.what: A phase is one round of testing in a given period. Test sheets and workshop tables always belong to a phase.
steps: Press Create phase and enter its name and period.
Set the status to Active when testing starts.
The phase code can be changed any time.

testCases.title: Test scenarios
testCases.what: The steps to try and the expected results. Results are recorded in Test sheets or at workshop tables.
steps: Press Create test scenario to write one.
For many at once, use Import from Excel.
Tick several scenarios to change them together.

imports.title: Import from Excel
imports.what: Bring in many test scenarios or problems at once from an Excel file. Nothing is saved before you approve it.
steps: Upload an Excel or CSV file.
Check the rows marked with problems and choose what to do.
Press Apply to save.

workshop.title: Workshop & tables
workshop.what: Group testing per table with QR cards. Here you set up tables, follow progress, review incoming problems and set the public view.
steps: Create tables, choose their features and enter the members' names (and e-mails if any).
Print the table cards and hand them out.
Follow the progress board and review incoming problems during the workshop.

runs.title: Test sheets
runs.what: A test sheet holds the scenarios assigned to individual testers in a phase.
steps: Create a test sheet, then add test scenarios.
Assign scenarios to testers, then press Start.
When done, lock the test sheet once the results are approved.

execution.title: Trying a scenario
execution.what: Here you try one scenario and record the result.
steps: Follow its steps in the service under test.
Choose As expected, Not as expected, or Could not try.
For Not as expected, describe what happened, attach a screenshot, then report the problem.

bugs.title: Problems
bugs.what: Every problem found, with its impact, priority and fix status.
steps: Open a problem to see its details, photos and history.
Developers update the status while fixing; testers check again.
Tick several problems to change them together.

evidence.title: Photos & evidence
evidence.what: All screenshots, documents and notes that prove the results in this project.
steps: Filter by type or keyword.
Open a file to see where it is used.

reports.title: Reports
reports.what: A summary of testing results and problems for leaders, and data downloads.
steps: Choose filters, e.g. phase or feature.
Download as Excel or CSV under Export data.
See the Activity log to know who changed what.

members.title: Members & tasks
members.what: Who takes part in this project and their task: Tester, Developer or Observer.
steps: Add people by e-mail; without an account, enter their name.
Send an activation link to accounts that are not active yet.
Change someone's task; you will be asked to confirm.

settings.title: Features & groups
settings.what: The features (parts of the service under test) and scenario groups of this project.
steps: Add features before writing test scenarios.
Feature codes can be changed; existing scenario codes stay.

adminUsers.title: Users
adminUsers.what: All accounts on this website. The Super Admin creates accounts and sets their roles.
steps: Create an account and choose a role: User, Admin or Super Admin.
Change a role with the choice on each row; you will be asked to confirm.
Create a reset link when someone forgets their password.

adminProjects.title: Manage projects
adminProjects.what: All projects on this website, archived ones included.
steps: Change a project's name, code or description.
Archive finished projects; their content stays readable.

adminRecovery.title: Account recovery
adminRecovery.what: "Forgot password" and "Forgot e-mail" requests from users.
steps: Check who is asking through the contact they gave.
Create a reset link and send it to them.
Mark the request as done.

adminSettings.title: Website settings
adminSettings.what: Settings for the whole website: name, announcement, help contact and sign-in time limits.
steps: Change a value and save.
The announcement shows at the top of every page.

adminAudit.title: Website activity log
adminAudit.what: A record of who did what and when, across the website.
steps: Filter by project, type or date.
Open an entry to see the detailed changes.

guide.title: Guide
guide.what: The full illustrated guide, arranged by role.
steps: Choose the part that fits your role in the contents.

search.title: Search this project
search.what: Finds test scenarios, problems and test sheets at once by their title or code.
